state.projectTitle: Void Studio: SDLC Office Materialization Simulator
state.organisation: Istanbul Kültür University, Computer Engineering Dept.
state.targetPopulation: COM0463 IT Project Management students (3rd/4th year undergraduates, n≈35)
state.problemStatement: In COM0463, a lot of students know the SDLC in theory but do not really see how one bad decision can affect later phases. In 2025, around 72% of student projects went over their original time estimate by more than 40%. From project reviews, it looked like students treated requirements, design, implementation, testing, and deployment as separate tasks instead of connected stages. This project tries to make that clearer by putting the whole SDLC into one simulation where the player manages budget, morale, technical debt, and time. The main idea is that early mistakes should create visible problems later.
state.deliverableJust: I chose a browser-based 3D simulation because it can show project consequences immediately instead of only explaining them in class. The resource bars connect game actions to real PM ideas like budget pressure, time pressure, and technical debt. It also makes it easier to review student decisions after the session. The local AI part is optional and mainly adds more event variety, but the game can still work without it.
inScope: 6-phase SDLC progression (Requirements → Design → Implementation → Testing → Deployment → Maintenance)
3D isometric office materialization from void using Three.js
4-resource management system (Budget, Morale, Technical Debt, Time)
Dynamic event system with 15+ predefined scenarios and AI-generated events
Local LLM integration (Phi-3.5 Mini via WebLLM) for adaptive game mastering
Decision cards with visible trade-off impacts per option
Phase transition animations with office unlock sequences
NPC character system with mood-based contextual dialogue
Victory/Game Over conditions with score summary
Fallback mode for environments without GPU/WebGPU
outScope: Cloud-hosted LLM inference (all local via WebLLM)
Real financial data or production project imports

frs.desc: System shall simulate 6 SDLC phases (Requirements, Design, Implementation, Testing, Deployment, Maintenance) in sequential order with task checklists per phase.
System shall track 4 resource metrics (Budget, Morale, Technical Debt, Time) with real-time animated HUD bars that update after every action.
System shall trigger contextual random events during gameplay with 3 decision options, each showing predicted resource impacts before selection.
System shall materialize 3D office furniture and space from the void upon completing each SDLC phase, using particle effects and opacity animations.
System shall provide an AI Game Master mode using a local Phi-3.5 Mini LLM (via WebLLM) to generate dynamic events, evaluate decisions, and produce NPC dialogue.
System shall fall back to predefined event logic when LLM is unavailable, ensuring full playability without AI.
System shall end the game in 'Game Over' when any critical resource reaches 0% (or Tech Debt reaches 100%), displaying a post-mortem with final score.
System shall display a Victory screen with score breakdown when all 6 SDLC phases are completed successfully.
System shall provide a 'Consult AI' button allowing players to request strategic advice from the LLM about their current resource state.
System shall support NPC characters (PM Senior, Tech Lead, QA Manager, UX Designer) with personality-driven mood responses based on game state.

System shall log all player actions (task completions, event triggers, decision choices, resource deltas, phase transitions) to browser localStorage with timestamps for post-session analytics and instructor review.
System shall export a JSON session log file containing anonymised gameplay data that the instructor can import into the GPPT analytics dashboard for cohort-level analysis.

nfrs.desc: 3D scene shall render at ≥30 FPS on mid-range hardware (Intel i5, integrated GPU). The renderer shall degrade gracefully on WebGL-unsupported environments.
A new player shall be able to understand the HUD, execute their first task, and resolve their first event within 3 minutes without external instruction.
Game shall run in Chrome 113+, Firefox 115+, and Edge 113+ without plugins or installation. WebLLM requires WebGPU; game works without it.
LLM event generation shall complete within 10 seconds. If LLM response exceeds 30 seconds, system shall timeout and use fallback logic.
All UI text shall maintain WCAG AA contrast ratio (4.5:1). Decision options shall be keyboard-navigable.

System shall comply with KVKK (Turkish data protection law) and GDPR principles: no personally identifiable information (PII) shall be collected or transmitted. All gameplay data remains in the player's browser localStorage. Session logs exported for instructor review shall be anonymised with opaque session IDs only.

Players shall provide informed consent via an in-game notice before any session data is logged. Players may clear all stored data at any time via browser settings. No data shall be sent to external servers without explicit opt-in.

sixDim.what: A single-player browser game where the student manages a software project across the full SDLC. The game has 6 phases, 4 main resources (budget, morale, technical debt, and time), and event cards with different choices. Finishing phases makes more of the office appear.
sixDim.why: The main reason for this design is to help students see that SDLC phases are connected. If the player rushes early work, they should feel the effect later through lower resources, more problems, and worse outcomes. I also wanted the game to be more active than a normal lecture or slide explanation.
sixDim.who: The main target is COM0463 students. It should especially fit students who like trying strategies, improving scores, and seeing clear feedback after each decision.
sixDim.when: It would be used during the SDLC and risk management part of COM0463. A normal session would be around 30 to 60 minutes.
sixDim.how: The project uses Three.js for the visual side and simple resource tracking for gameplay. Every decision shows its effect on the project. AI can be turned on for extra event variety, but there is also a fallback mode.
sixDim.where: The game runs in the browser on lab computers or student laptops. It does not need a full server setup for the main gameplay.

state.narrativeTheme: The player is a project manager building a software office out of an empty void. As the project goes well, the office slowly appears. If the player makes bad decisions, the office starts to break down again.
state.narrativeArc: At the start, there is almost nothing in the office. As the player moves through the SDLC, they unlock more parts of the space. The middle of the game becomes harder because resource problems start to build up. By the end, the player either finishes the project with a complete office or loses control because of low resources and high technical debt.
state.characters: Project Manager (student player): makes the main decisions. PM Senior: gives advice and warnings. Tech Lead: reacts to technical debt and shortcuts. QA Lead: reacts to testing and quality problems. UX Designer: reacts to morale and workload. Game Master: provides event text and feedback through AI or fallback logic.
state.storyWorld: The game takes place in a software company office that starts as an empty dark space. As the player manages the project better, more of the office appears. The world is simple on purpose so the player can connect project progress with visual progress.

conceptMappings.dynamic: Decisions in Phase 1 compound in Phase 5 — skipping requirements analysis triggers testing failures

conceptMappings.mechanic: Random event cards with 3 trade-off options showing resource impact before selection
conceptMappings.dynamic: Risk acceptance vs. mitigation under resource scarcity; wrong choice cascades
conceptMappings.rationale: Events force reactive decision-making under pressure, simulating the unpredictability of real projects

conceptMappings.mechanic: Budget/Time depletion per task + event impacts; 4 resource bars always visible
conceptMappings.dynamic: Scarcity forces prioritization; overspending on Phase 2 leaves nothing for Phase 5
conceptMappings.rationale: Budget and time are finite — exactly like real projects. Resource scarcity creates authentic PM decision-making pressure

mdaAnalysis.mechanics: Resource Bars (Budget/Morale/TechDebt/Time), Task Execution checklists, Decision Cards with 3 options and predicted impacts, Phase Progression gates, Office Materialization rewards, AI Event Generation (LLM), NPC Mood System, Session Logging.
mdaAnalysis.dynamics: Risk-vs-reward trade-offs at every decision. Resource scarcity creates genuine tension as players progress through SDLC phases — improving one resource often degrades another, mirroring real PM constraint dynamics. The void-to-office progression creates an escalation of commitment. Compounding TechDebt punishes shortcuts with cascading consequences in later phases. LLM-generated events inject realistic unpredictability.
mdaAnalysis.aesthetics: Challenge (managing 4 resources under SDLC phase pressure demands genuine PM knowledge), Strategy (long-horizon resource allocation mirrors real PM planning), Narrative (building a software company from nothing in the void), Discovery (watching the office emerge; encountering unique LLM-generated events), Sensation (3D particle effects and materialization animations).

state.introText: You are the project manager of a software company that starts in an empty void. As you complete each SDLC phase, more of the office appears. Your job is to manage the project, protect your resources, and finish the office before everything falls apart.

scenarios.name: The Requirements Meltdown
scenarios.title: Stakeholder Scope Creep
scenarios.setup: The primary stakeholder adds 5 new features mid-requirements phase. Budget is at 85%, Morale at 75%.
scenarios.objective: Manage scope without destroying budget or morale.
scenarios.winCondition: Budget > 60% AND Morale > 50% after resolving all scope requests within 5 decision turns
scenarios.storyboard: Event Card → Decision (Accept/Reject/Negotiate) → Resource Impact → NPC Reaction → Narrative Feedback
scenarios.outcome: Win (Budget>60%, Morale>50%): +100 + office expansion. Partial (Budget 30-60%): +50 + partial furniture. Fail: -20 + void reclaims.

activities.description: Stakeholder demands 5 new features. Student must negotiate partial scope reduction, deferring 3 features to Phase 2.
activities.trigger: Scope Creep event activates at turn 1
activities.winCondition: Negotiate selected; scope reduced to 2 features; Budget preserved > 60%
activities.loseCondition: Accept all 5 features; Budget drops below 40%
activities.loseResult: Budget crisis; TechDebt +10; cascade event next turn
activities.neutralCondition: Player negotiates partial scope reduction, preserving Budget > 40% but losing 2 features and consuming 1 day of Time
activities.neutralResult: +15 XP; scope partially managed; triangle stabilised

activities.description: Budget crisis worsening. Student must decide whether to escalate scope dispute to steering committee or handle internally.
activities.trigger: Budget drops below 50% at any turn
activities.winCondition: Escalation approved; committee defers 3 features; resource drain stopped
activities.loseResult: Time -2 turns; morale -5 from perceived failure
activities.neutralCondition: Committee defers decision — no immediate resource loss but 1 day of Time consumed and uncertainty remains

scenarios.name: The Deployment Disaster
scenarios.title: Production Server Crash
scenarios.setup: Deployment to production fails. Server crashes. Client is watching. TechDebt at 45%.
scenarios.objective: Recover the deployment without losing the client's trust.
scenarios.winCondition: Deploy successfully with Morale > 40% and TechDebt < 70% within 5 decision turns
scenarios.storyboard: Crisis Alert → Emergency Options (Rollback/Hotfix/Communicate) → Triage → NPC Reactions → Resolution
scenarios.outcome: Win (deployed, Morale>40%): +150 + ops center materializes. Partial (deployed, Morale 20-40%): +80 + basic ops desk. Fail: Game Over.

activities.description: Server crashed after deployment. Student must decide between full rollback (safe but slow) or targeted hotfix (fast but risky).
activities.winCondition: Rollback succeeds; hotfix deployed; system stable; TechDebt +5 only
activities.loseCondition: Hotfix introduces regression; TechDebt +20; second cascade failure
activities.loseResult: System unstable; additional recovery turn required
activities.neutralCondition: Rollback succeeds but hotfix introduces minor regression — TechDebt +5 but system stable enough to continue

activities.description: Client is watching the failed deployment. Student must communicate the situation: full transparency, partial disclosure, or blame external factors.
activities.winCondition: Full transparency selected; client agrees to 1-day delay; relationship preserved
activities.winResult: +20 XP + Client Trust badge progress + Morale +5 (team respects honesty)
activities.loseCondition: Blame external factors; client demands audit; Morale -15
activities.loseResult: Trust eroded; additional oversight imposed; future events more severe
activities.neutralCondition: Client agrees to 1-day delay — Time -1 day but relationship preserved and team morale stable

scenarios.name: The Technical Debt Avalanche
scenarios.title: Legacy Code Collapse
scenarios.setup: Technical debt accumulated from rushed Implementation phase causes cascading test failures in Testing. TechDebt at 65%.
scenarios.objective: Reduce TechDebt below 50% before Deployment phase begins.
scenarios.winCondition: TechDebt < 50% AND Time > 20% after refactoring sprint within 4 decision turns
scenarios.storyboard: Debt Alert → Triage (Full Refactor/Targeted Fix/Accept and Ship) → Resource Consequence → NPC Reactions → Outcome
scenarios.outcome: Win (TechDebt<50%): +120 + clean testing room. Partial (TechDebt 50-65%): +60 + partial QA desk. Fail: Deployment blocked.

activities.description: TechDebt at 65%. Student must decide: full refactor (expensive, slow, thorough) or targeted hotspot fixing (cheap, fast, partial).
activities.winCondition: Full refactor reduces TechDebt to <40%; codebase clean; Time -3 days, Budget -15%
activities.loseCondition: Budget insufficient for full refactor; TechDebt remains high
activities.neutralCondition: Partial refactor reduces TechDebt by 15% but consumes 3 extra days of Time — enough to continue but not ideal
activities.neutralResult: +18 XP; TechDebt reduced partially; timeline compressed

scoringSystem.bonuses: Perfect Phase: Complete a phase with all resources above 60%: +25. Void Conqueror: Complete all 6 phases: +100. AI Advisor: Use LLM advisor at least 3 times: +15. Zero Debt: Finish with TechDebt < 15%: +50.
scoringSystem.penalties: TechDebt above 80% at game end halves the final score. Game Over (any resource at 0%) nullifies phase completion bonuses.
scoringSystem.badges: Void Pioneer (Phase 1), Code Commander (Phase 3), Ship Captain (Phase 5), Office Architect (all 6 phases), Chaos Survivor (10+ events), Budget Guardian (Budget > 70%), Zero Debt Master (TechDebt < 15%)

rewardTiers.elite: Office Architect (all 6 phases, Score ≥ 400): 5-pt course bonus + 'Master PM' digital certificate
rewardTiers.professional: Deployment Survivor (reach Phase 5, Score ≥ 250): 3-pt course bonus + 'Senior PM' badge
rewardTiers.access: Void Explorer (complete any 2 phases): Participation credit + understanding of SDLC phases

tuslerRisks.risk: Ignoring technical debt in Implementation phase leads to cascading test failures
tuslerRisks.mitigation: TechDebt bar visible at all times with colour-coded warnings (green/yellow/red); events explicitly warn about compounding consequences in subsequent phases
tuslerRisks.responsive: Recovery events offer debt-reduction sprints at cost of budget/time; instructor can trigger manual debt-reduction event

tuslerRisks.risk: Budget depletion before Deployment phase prevents project completion
tuslerRisks.mitigation: Budget impact shown numerically on every decision card before selection; cumulative spend tracker in HUD
tuslerRisks.responsive: Emergency budget events and contractor options available in late phases; instructor can inject emergency funding scenario

tuslerRisks.risk: Game difficulty too steep — students never reach Phase 4 Testing
tuslerRisks.mitigation: Difficulty dynamically scales with resource state: resources below 30% trigger more recovery-oriented events; early phases have gentler event probability
tuslerRisks.responsive: Instructor can adjust base event probability in Events.js configuration; playtesting calibrates difficulty curve

tuslerRisks.risk: LLM model download (1.5GB) blocks gameplay on slow lab connections
tuslerRisks.mitigation: LLM is fully optional — game is 100% playable via FallbackLogic.js predefined events; toggle clearly visible on loading screen
tuslerRisks.responsive: One-time download cached by browser ServiceWorker; lab admin can pre-cache model on lab machines before session

tuslerRisks.risk: Students focus on winning game rather than learning PM concepts
tuslerRisks.mitigation: Score formula weights all 4 resources equally preventing single-metric gaming; mandatory post-game reflection checkpoint
tuslerRisks.responsive: Post-session debrief discussion led by instructor comparing in-game decisions to PMBOK frameworks and Marchewka chapters

tuslerRisks.risk: WebGL rendering fails on older lab hardware without discrete GPU
tuslerRisks.mitigation: Canvas 2D fallback renderer implemented with graceful degradation; game detects WebGL capability at startup
tuslerRisks.responsive: IT support notified to enable hardware acceleration in browser settings; software rendering fallback provides starfield visual

tuslerRisks.risk: Simulation events do not accurately represent real SDLC challenges
tuslerRisks.mitigation: All events reviewed by course instructor against Marchewka chapters 6-11 and PMBOK risk categories before deployment
tuslerRisks.responsive: Event library updated each semester based on instructor feedback and student post-session surveys

tuslerRisks.risk: Student data privacy breach through exported session logs
tuslerRisks.mitigation: No PII collected; session IDs are opaque UUIDs; KVKK/GDPR compliance built into NFR-06/NFR-07; consent notice shown before logging
tuslerRisks.responsive: All localStorage data can be cleared by student at any time; exported logs contain no identifying information

tuslerRisks.risk: AI-generated events produce pedagogically inappropriate or unbalanced content
tuslerRisks.mitigation: LLM prompts constrained with JSON schema enforcement; resource impact values clamped to ±25 range; all AI outputs validated against schema before display
tuslerRisks.responsive: Fallback events used if validation fails; instructor can disable AI mode mid-session

state.gamePurpose: Help COM0463 students practise SDLC management and project decision-making in a more active way.
state.gameSubject: SDLC management, risk, resources, stakeholder problems, and technical debt.
state.gameMethod: The game gets harder over time, and early choices affect later results. The office-building idea is used as a visual reward so progress is easy to see.
state.gameMeasurement: Learning would be checked with a quiz, reflection, and later coursework.
state.gamePlayers: COM0463 IT Project Management students, Year 3/4, n≈35
state.gamePoints: +Score for resource preservation across phases. Budget saved = Budget score. Low TechDebt = TechDebt score. Phase completion = +50 per phase. Event survival = +10 per event.
state.gameAchievements: Office Architect: complete all 6 SDLC phases. Chaos Survivor: survive 10+ events. Budget Guardian: finish with Budget > 70%. Zero Debt: finish with TechDebt < 15%.
state.gameBadges: Void Pioneer (Phase 1), Code Commander (Phase 3), Ship Captain (Phase 5), Office Architect (all 6 phases), Master PM (Score ≥ 400).
state.gameOverview: A browser-based 3D simulation for COM0463 where students manage a project across the SDLC and slowly build an office by making better decisions.
state.sdtAutonomy: Students can choose how carefully or aggressively they want to manage the project. They are not forced into one strategy, so they can test different approaches and see the results.
state.sdtCompetence: When students make better decisions, they protect their resources and make visible progress in the game. This gives immediate feedback and helps them see improvement.
state.sdtRelatedness: NPC reactions and class discussion after the session help students feel that their decisions affect a team, not just a score counter.
state.howEthics: Participation should be voluntary, and a non-game alternative should be available if needed. Any collected data should be anonymised and used only for teaching and evaluation.
state.logPrivacy: Logs should avoid personal data and use anonymous session IDs. Students should be told what is stored and should be able to clear local data.
state.platform: Browser-based web application built with JavaScript and Three.js. No installation is needed for normal use.
state.instructorRole: The instructor should mainly guide reflection and ask students why they made certain decisions instead of directly playing the game for them.
state.gameDurationRules: No single game should exceed 60 minutes of active gameplay. Total session including introduction and debrief: 60 minutes. Recommended timing: Introduction 5 min + Active gameplay 45 min + Debrief & reflection 10 min. Instructor may pause at any time for teaching moments.

dataCollectionPlan.method: Automated browser localStorage logging + JSON export
dataCollectionPlan.analysis: Post-session: resource trajectory analysis, phase dropout patterns, event resolution quality; cohort comparison with pre-simulation baseline

socialInteraction.collaboration: Post-session score comparisons create peer discussion about SDLC management strategies; students explain their resource management approaches during debrief.
socialInteraction.competition: Session leaderboard (optional) creates competitive comparison of SDLC management quality; score tier visibility drives performance benchmarking.
socialInteraction.communityBuilding: Post-session debrief discussion where students compare strategies builds shared understanding of COM0463 SDLC theory; different outcomes generate authentic peer discussion.

gameDynamics.progressionSystems: Game structured in 6 SDLC phases, each with phase-specific tasks and events. Resource thresholds tighten as the project advances. Phase completion triggers office materialization. Victory/Game Over determines final score and badge awards.
gameDynamics.feedbackLoops: Real-time resource HUD provides continuous visual feedback on all 4 dimensions. Event outcomes provide immediate consequence feedback. Phase transition triggers materialization animation as checkpoint. Final score breakdown provides comprehensive PM decision quality assessment.
gameDynamics.competition: Optional post-session leaderboard by score tier (Score ≥ 400 / 250 / < 250). Weekly Office Architect badge for completing all 6 phases. Class-wide score distribution displayed post-session to stimulate SDLC strategy discussion.
gameDynamics.collaboration: Post-session peer comparison and debrief discussion. Future: team mode pairing PM + Tech Lead roles.
gameDynamics.adaptability: Event probability and severity configurable per SDLC phase. AI Game Master adapts event context to current resource state. Fallback mode uses predefined events of equivalent quality.
